title: The Tooth They Drilled — Neolithic Mehrgarh Flint Bow-Drills, Villabruna Bitumen & Lonche Beeswax Dental Fillings Under SEM & Synchrotron Micro-CT

teenKit.tldr: Long before modern clinics, Novocaine, or stainless steel tools, ancient humans in Neolithic Pakistan were using flint bow-drills to painstakingly bore holes into infected molars to stop agonizing toothaches.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that the desperate, brutal human drive to fix our own bodies and conquer pain is thousands of years older than written history itself.
keyTakeaways: Neolithic dentists at Mehrgarh used specialized flint bow-drills to drill precisely into human molars over 8,000 years ago.
Advanced high-tech imaging like scanning electron microscopes (SEM) and synchrotron micro-CT reveal microscopic drill striations and ancient fillings invisible to the naked eye.
Prehistoric dental care wasn't just drilling; discoveries like the Lonche beeswax filling show ancient people also used natural antiseptics and sealants to patch cavities.

vocab.meaning: The study of human remains from archaeological sites to understand what ancient people ate, how they lived, and what diseases they suffered from.
An insanely powerful X-ray machine that creates ultra-detailed 3D digital scans of microscopic structures inside ancient bones and teeth without destroying them.
A primitive tool using a bowstring wrapped around a shaft to spin a sharp flint tip at high speeds, used by ancient humans for making fire and drilling teeth.
Tiny, parallel scratch marks left behind on a surface by a tool, which scientists use like microscopic fingerprints to figure out what instrument was used.

quiz.question: What tool did ancient dentists at Mehrgarh use to drill into human molars during the Neolithic period?
quiz.explanation: Archaeologists found concentric microscopic striations proving they used precision flint bow-drills.

quiz.question: What high-tech method allows scientists to scan the internal contents of ancient teeth without cracking them open?
quiz.explanation: Synchrotron micro-CT uses high-powered particle accelerator X-rays to map out internal structures in exquisite 3D detail.

quiz.question: What ancient material was discovered functioning as an ancient filling in a 6,500-year-old tooth at Lonche?
quiz.explanation: FTIR and radiocarbon testing verified that ancient people used beeswax as an adhesive seal or filling inside a cavity.
